items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: And the band that I joined was the band with Lee Morgan, Benny Golson, Wynton Kelly, Melba Liston was the musical director

ctx.x: Hearing your note in place with everything else, I mean really helps your ear doesn’t it?

It does. And you hear the resolutions of the harmony, harmony of arrangements that are written by great arrangers. I remember when I played with the Dizzy Gillespie group and I was playing arrangements by Quincy Jones, by Dizzy himself, Ernie Wilkins, Melba Liston, Benny Golson. You learn about resolutions in the big group, because you hear all these resolving harmonies and things. So when you improvise you also use resolutions as a big part of the way that you make an improvisation.
That’s a great point. When you were growing up, did you have a musical family?

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yeah, with Dizzy’s big band... Benny Golson was there... I had to go there anyway.

ctx.x: Yeah, with Dizzy’s big band. That band was way over my head, but I had to go there anyway. Benny Golson was there, and Lee Morgan, Wynton Kelly. Melba Liston was the musical director. I had to go there. I had to go there and get kicked, kicked and beat-up on. I did it. They taught me a lot in there.
How long were you with Dizzy in its first incarnation?
